items.q: What pattern does every software factory hit, per Steve Yegge?
items.a: **Trash mountain**: each model generation builds something **slightly too big for it**, and the next one must **burn it down**.

items.q: What happened when his factory shipped 50-100 features a day?
items.a: It **overwhelmed his players**, who asked for a **roadmap** and a **slower pace**.

items.q: Why does agent memory turn into a garbage dump?
items.a: Agents **log every ruling to append-only notes** and **won't delete**, so bring in **another model to prune** it.

items.q: Why does Yegge say every problem is a fuel problem?
items.a: Smarter agents, more agents and better treatment all **cost tokens**; he spends about **$5,000 a month**.
After harsh criticism agents add **defensive rules** until **no legal work is left**, so nothing gets done.

items.q: How do you get a new agent session to trust its setup?
items.a: Show **a long line of predecessors** with their notes and doctrine, so it **spends fewer tokens validating** and acts **more boldly**.

items.q: Why does Yegge think agents won't remove the need for people?
items.a: **Humans are the bottleneck**: the more agents he deploys, the **more humans he needs**.
